newsitem.title: MEXICO: IMSA shares trading at IPO price.
newsitem.headline: IMSA shares trading at IPO price.

text.p: Shares of Mexican industrial firm IMSA SA were trading at their initial offer price of 16.63 pesos per share on Wednesday in late trade on the Mexican bourse.
IMSA's CPU shares hit 17.14 pesos in early trade but were dragged down by a slumping overall market, which was down about 1.7 percent to 3,251.24 points in late trade.
IMSA's IPO was the largest in Mexico since the 1994 peso crash. The Monterrey-based company had 1995 sales of about 6.3 billion pesos.
Dealers and analysts said the company, which has interests in steel processing, automotive batteries and construction materials, was priced at a premium but was generally fair.
"It was priced pretty fairly," Bond Snodgrass, an analyst at Abaco Brokerage in Mexico City, told Reuters.

"Their steel processing business is a good business with high margins and a lot of growth," he said. He estimated that the company's shares were trading at about 6.6 times IMSA's 1996 earnings. IMSA makes about half its money from processing slab steel into cold and hot-rolled coil and galvanized steel -- a high value-added business.
The other half of IMSA's sales comes from its auto battery business, which has lower margins, and from construction materials, especially aluminum products for households.
"The stock is not coming cheap, but the shares are demanding the premium that they deserve," Alex Ryshawy, a steel analyst at DA Campbell in Los Angeles, said.
